I'm happy to announce that **hal** is now on CRAN:

```{r}
install.packages("hal")
```

hal is a coding agent for R. It isn't another chat panel. It gives you an
agent you call from R code. It can read your files, search your project,
run R in your session, look at your plots, and hand results back as
ordinary R objects you can pipe, test, and script.

## Why another AI package?

Coding agents like GitHub Copilot and Claude Code are very capable, but they
were built for a terminal or an IDE sidebar. R users work in a console,
next to live data frames, models, and plots. An agent that can't see
`df` is guessing.

hal connects the two. It talks directly to the agent tools you already
have, and it adds R-specific pieces: an `eval_r` tool that runs code in your
session, pipe-friendly verbs, verified transforms, and plot capture. It
needs **no API keys**, because it uses the Copilot or Claude subscription
you already pay for.

## Three verbs

### `hal()`: have a conversation

A stateful, multi-turn session with full agent tool access:

```{r}
library(hal)
hal_setup()   # picks the right backend for your setup

hal("What are the top 3 dplyr verbs and when would I use each?")
hal("Show me a filter example")
```

Add `use_env = TRUE` and the agent can inspect live objects in your
session instead of guessing at them:

```{r}
df <- mtcars
hal("Which rows in df have above-median mpg?", use_env = TRUE)
```

### `hal_ask()`: analyze mid-pipe

Pipe any object in, get analysis printed, and your data flows through
unchanged:

```{r}
mtcars |>
  hal_ask("What patterns stand out in fuel efficiency? 3 bullets.")
```

<img src="https://arclite-red.github.io/hal/reference/figures/demo-pipe-ask.gif" alt="hal_ask demo" width="100%" />

### `hal_do()`: transform mid-pipe, with a receipt

`hal_do()` generates R code, runs it, and returns the result. It then
checks what changed:

```{r}
mtcars |>
  hal_do("group by cylinder count, summarize mean mpg and mean hp")
#> i hal_do: 32 -> 3 rows | -9 cols (...) | +2 cols (mean_mpg, mean_hp)
```

Every transform gets a structural report covering row deltas, added or
dropped columns, class changes, and new `NA`s. Suspicious results, such as
output identical to the input or zero rows, raise a warning. In scripts
that run non-interactively, failures abort instead of passing bad data
downstream quietly.

<img src="https://arclite-red.github.io/hal/reference/figures/demo-pipe-do.gif" alt="hal_do demo" width="100%" />

In RStudio or Positron, `hal_do()` can also replace itself in your editor
with the code it generated. You keep the code, and the agent isn't needed
next time you run the script.

## Two things I haven't seen elsewhere

**`hal_excel()` turns a spreadsheet into a verified R script.** It reads an
`.xlsx`, translates each formula column into a tidyverse expression, and
then checks every translation against the values Excel cached for that
column, row by row. Columns that match go into a runnable `mutate()`
pipeline. Anything that doesn't match is left as a commented stub for you
to review, never silently guessed.

```{r}
hal_excel("sales_model.xlsx")
#> v revenue: verified (120/120 rows match Excel)
#> v margin: verified (120/120 rows match Excel)
```

**Plot vision.** When the agent draws a plot through `eval_r`, hal captures
it and sends the image back to the model. "Make this publication-ready"
then works on what the chart actually looks like, not on what the code
suggests it might look like.

## Pick your backend

The same R API runs over three backends, and your code doesn't change
when you switch:

| Backend | What it uses | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| **vscode** (default in Positron) | Positron's built-in language models via a bundled bridge extension | No extra install; reuses your Positron Copilot sign-in |
| **copilot** | GitHub Copilot CLI | Many models, mid-session model switching, Plan/Autopilot modes |
| **claude** | Claude Code CLI | Claude subscription users; quota visibility with `hal_quota()` |

```{r}
hal_configure(backend = "claude")
hal_status()   # traffic-light check that tells you the next step
```

## Guardrails

An agent that runs code in your session needs limits. hal includes:

- an `eval_r` denylist enforced by walking the code's syntax tree, not by
  matching strings;
- a credential scanner on outbound text that can warn, redact, or block;
- permission policies (`"auto-allow"`, `"auto-deny"`, `"ask"`, or your
  own R function);
- classed conditions (`hal_error`, `hal_do_error`, ...) so you can catch
  failures programmatically.

The [safety guide](https://arclite-red.github.io/hal/articles/safety.html)
covers each of these.

## Make your own tools

Any R function can become a tool the agent can call:

```{r}
hal_register_tool(
  fun = function(ticker) paste("$142.50 for", ticker),
  name = "stock_price",
  description = "Get current stock price",
  types = list(ticker = "string")
)
hal("What's the stock price of AAPL?")
```

## Try it and tell me what breaks

```{r}
install.packages("hal")
library(hal)
hal_setup()
hal("Hello!")
```
